title: A strictly standard element inverts to a smooth algebra
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] and let $a\in A$ be strictly standard in $A$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element]. Then the localization $A_a$ of $A$ at $\{1,a,a^2,\dots\}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], an $R$-algebra via $R\to A\to A_a$, is a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07CA (lemma-elkik, line 253), first paragraph of its proof (lines 261-276: 'Assume a is strictly standard in A over R. We claim that A_a is smooth over R')
